title: Auto-sync OpenCode session title with current branch
body:
## Summary
Session titles are no longer consistently renamed to match the active git branch, which breaks tab/session distinguishability in parallel worktree workflows.

## Problem
- `pre-edit-check.sh` auto-syncs terminal tab title but does not auto-sync OpenCode session title.
- `session-rename-helper.sh sync-branch` defaults to globally most-recent session when no session ID is passed, which can target the wrong session in parallel usage.

## Proposed fix
1. Make `session-rename-helper.sh sync-branch` resolve default session by current working directory first, then fallback to global most-recent session.
2. Add non-blocking auto-call in `pre-edit-check.sh` to sync session title with branch when running inside OpenCode.
3. Keep MCP tool path (`session-rename_sync_branch`) unchanged; this fix restores practical auto behavior even when explicit tool calls are skipped.
---

title: full-loop: enforce mode-aware signature provenance in PR bodies
body:
## Summary
The /full-loop guidance currently allows signatures that omit explicit session provenance when PR bodies are created from worker/subagent contexts.

## Problem
PR descriptions can include the aidevops footer without the time/tokens sentence, reducing auditability and making self-activity detection weaker.

## Proposed fix
Update /full-loop documentation to require mode-aware footer arguments:
- interactive: issue + session-type interactive
- headless worker: no-session + session-type worker + explicit elapsed time
- optional tokens only when telemetry is available
- verification that final PR body contains aidevops signature and time provenance text

## Acceptance criteria
- Full-loop command doc includes explicit interactive and headless footer invocations
- Instructions include provenance verification check for PR body
- Guidance avoids fabricated token values

title: Bug: should_overwrite_user_file undefined in migrations.sh — causes exit 5 during install
body:
## Summary

Fresh install via `bash <(curl -fsSL https://aidevops.sh/install)` fails at the end of the migration phase with:

```
./setup-modules/migrations.sh: line 74: should_overwrite_user_file: command not found
./setup-modules/migrations.sh: line 94: should_overwrite_user_file: command not found
[ERROR] ./setup-modules/migrations.sh:595 exit 5
[ERROR] ./setup-modules/migrations.sh:595 exit 5
```

## Root Cause

The function `should_overwrite_user_file()` was originally defined in `setup.sh` (added in 08f2a632b, PR #2725) but was **removed** in 6d6279379 (PR #2728, feature toggles refactor) without being re-added to `shared-constants.sh` or any other sourced module.

`migrations.sh` still calls the function on lines 74 and 94 (inside the oh-my-opencode cleanup migration), so it fails with `command not found`. Combined with `set -Eeuo pipefail` and the ERR trap, this produces exit code 5.

## Impact

- The error occurs during an optional oh-my-opencode cleanup migration, so **core install completes successfully** despite the errors.
- However, the error output is confusing for new users and may cause them to think the install failed.
- Any migration steps that run *after* the failing function call in `run_migrations()` may be skipped due to `errexit`.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. **Restore** `should_overwrite_user_file()` in `setup.sh` or `shared-constants.sh` (as it was before PR #2728 removed it), or
2. **Replace** the two calls in `migrations.sh` lines 74/94 with a simpler guard (e.g. check `OVERWRITE_MODE` directly or use `is_feature_enabled`), since the feature-toggle system from PR #2728 was meant to supersede this function.

## Environment

- Fresh install on Ubuntu (WSL2)
- Install method: `bash <(curl -fsSL https://aidevops.sh/install)`
- Repo cloned to `~/Git/aidevops/` at current HEAD of `main`

title: Bug: migrations.sh jq path fails with exit 5 when .mcp is missing
body:
## Summary
`setup-modules/migrations.sh` exits with code 5 in `_migrate_mcp_npx_to_binary` when `opencode.json` does not contain `.mcp` (e.g. minimal config `{}`).

## Reproduction
1. Use minimal config file:
   ```json
   {}
   ```
2. Run setup/migration path that executes `_migrate_mcp_npx_to_binary`.
3. Observe hard failure from jq query at `setup-modules/migrations.sh:595`.

## Expected
Migration should treat missing `.mcp` as empty and continue safely.

## Actual
jq query assumes `.mcp` exists and aborts, bubbling up as exit 5.

## Root Cause
Strict jq path in migration code does not guard optional object presence.

## Proposed Fix
Harden jq expression to tolerate missing `.mcp`, e.g. `(.mcp // {}) | to_entries[]? ...` and add regression test for minimal config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Minimal `opencode.json` (`{}`) does not fail migration.
- Existing migration behavior for populated `.mcp` remains unchanged.
- Regression test added for missing `.mcp` path.

Related: #14208

title: pulse: recover failed launch claims and block telemetry dispatch candidates
body:
## Summary
- Launch validation failures can leave issues assigned + `status:queued` without a running worker, reducing effective capacity.
- Historical "Dispatching worker" comments can continue to block redispatch after claim state has already been cleared.
- Supervisor/persistent telemetry issues can surface in fallback candidate lists and should be blocked deterministically.

## Scope
- Recover issue state on launch-validation failure when no worker appears.
- Treat dispatch comments as blocking only when issue is actively claimed.
- Exclude cross-runner queued issues from local `queued_without_worker` underfill pressure.
- Add hard guard in `dispatch_with_dedup` to block non-dispatchable management/telemetry issues.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Failed launch paths clear stale self-claim/queued state and re-open availability safely.
- No stale dispatch-comment blocks once active claim labels/assignee are gone.
- `queued_without_worker` does not count queued issues assigned to other runners.
- Telemetry/supervisor/persistent issues cannot be dispatched via `dispatch_with_dedup`.


---

title: Fix duplicate simplification issues under concurrent pulse runners
body:
## Problem

The simplification scan occasionally creates duplicate `simplification-debt` issues with the exact same title seconds apart.

## Evidence

Recent open duplicates in `marcusquinn/aidevops` show same-title pairs created near-simultaneously by different runners.

## Root cause

A cross-runner TOCTOU race in `pulse-wrapper.sh`: both runners can pass the pre-create dedup check before either issue is visible to the other, then both call `gh issue create`.

## Proposed fix

Add immediate post-create convergence in the simplification creation path:
- Query open simplification issues by exact title
- Keep newest issue
- Auto-close older same-title duplicates

Apply this for both markdown simplification and shell complexity issue creation paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- Concurrent creates converge to one open issue per exact title
- Existing pre-create dedup remains in place
- `shellcheck` passes on `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`

title: bug: restore pulse dispatch for maintainer-owned inactive backlog
body:
## Summary
- Pulse throughput is severely under target despite a large live backlog (`384+` open issues and `62` unmerged PRs observed in-session).
- Maintainer-owned inactive backlog is being treated as actively claimed, so the supervisor reports little or no dispatchable work and leaves worker slots idle.
- This regression affects shared pulse / worker behavior and likely suppresses throughput for other aidevops users as well.

## Root cause
- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is_assigned()` blocks on any non-self assignee, including repo owner / maintainer, even when the issue has no active claim state.
- Pulse candidate discovery is biased toward unassigned issues, so maintainer-owned inactive backlog is invisible to dispatch.
- `quality-feedback-helper.sh` creates fresh quality-debt issues already assigned to the repo owner, feeding the starvation loop.

## Acceptance criteria
- Owner/maintainer assignment is treated as passive backlog ownership unless the issue is actively claimed via `status:queued` or `status:in-progress`.
- Pulse candidate discovery and runnable-count logic include inactive maintainer-owned backlog.
- Fresh quality-debt issues are created in a dispatchable state instead of being hidden behind passive assignment.
- Regression tests cover both passive-owner visibility and active-claim duplicate protection.

## Evidence
- Live runtime check showed `active=1`, `max=24`, with a large backlog still open.
- Current regression test for assignee semantics failed before the fix.
- Patched logic raises live runnable count materially by reclassifying passive maintainer-owned backlog as dispatchable.

title: bug: detach worker stdio so deterministic fill can dispatch multiple slots
body:
## Summary
- Live monitoring after v3.5.466 shows the deterministic fill floor only dispatching one worker per pass even when `available=4` and `candidates=184`.
- The most likely cause is `dispatch_with_dedup()` launching workers in the background without detaching stdin/stdout/stderr.
- When deterministic fill iterates candidates from a process substitution, the first worker can inherit that stdin and consume the remaining candidate stream, aborting the loop early.

## Evidence
- `pulse.log` recorded `Deterministic fill floor: available=4 ... candidates=184` followed by `Deterministic fill floor complete: dispatched=1, target_available=4`.
- Live runtime runs launched real workers and PRs, but only one additional worker per fill pass.
- Background worker output leaked into the invoking shell output during runtime verification, consistent with missing stdio isolation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Worker launches from `dispatch_with_dedup()` detach stdin from candidate loops (`</dev/null`).
- Worker stdout/stderr are redirected to per-issue temp logs so launch validation reads the intended files and shell output stays clean.
- Runtime verification shows deterministic fill can dispatch multiple workers in one pass when capacity and candidates allow.
---

title: Bug: deterministic pulse fill floor skips runnable issues
body:
## Summary
`dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` returned `DISPATCHED=0` during this pulse even though `list_dispatchable_issue_candidates "marcusquinn/aidevops" 40` returned 5 runnable issues and manual `dispatch_with_dedup` calls launched workers successfully.

## Evidence
- Capacity check before dispatch: `MAX_WORKERS=24`, `WORKER_COUNT=0`, `AVAILABLE=24`
- Candidate prefilter returned issues `#14835`, `#14834`, `#14833`, `#14832`, `#14831`
- Manual dispatch launched 5 active workers for those issues immediately afterward
- The helper stdout was polluted by internal debug output from `count_runnable_candidates` / `count_queued_without_worker`, which may be related

## Impact
The supervisor can underfill the worker pool when it relies on the deterministic backfill helper.

title: Pulse bug: active worker detection misses live headless-runtime-helper wrappers
body:
## Summary
- The live pulse worker-counting path still misses active headless worker wrappers.
- In current production state, process-level evidence and the dispatch ledger show an in-flight worker, while pulse helper counts report zero active workers.

## Evidence
- `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh status` showed `issue-14939` in-flight with live PID `38455`.
- `ps -Ao pid,ppid,etime,command | rg 'headless-runtime-helper.sh run|Issue #14939'` showed the worker wrapper processes still running.
- At the same time, `source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh && list_active_worker_processes && count_active_workers` returned no active worker processes and `COUNT_ACTIVE=0`.

## Why it matters
- Pulse capacity calculations depend on active worker counts.
- Under-counting active workers can distort refill decisions and make concurrency accounting untrustworthy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Reproduce the mismatch with a deterministic test fixture or regression harness.
- Update worker detection so active headless-runtime-helper wrapper processes are counted reliably.
- Add regression coverage for wrapper-only and wrapper+child process states.

title: Pulse cleanup: remove debug stdout pollution from count_runnable_candidates and count_queued_without_worker
body:
## Summary
- The deterministic fill-floor fix now normalizes noisy count helper output, but the helper functions themselves still emit debug payloads to stdout.
- That leaves other callers and ad hoc diagnostics exposed to polluted numeric output.

## Evidence
- `count_runnable_candidates` currently emits repeated debug lines like `issue_count=0` / `pr_json='[]'` before the final numeric result.
- `count_queued_without_worker` currently emits large `queued_json='[...]'` payloads before the numeric result.
- The original `GH#14836` bug existed because callers consumed these helpers as if they returned clean integers.

## Why it matters
- Polluted stdout is still a correctness hazard for any caller that expects a numeric return.
- Large debug payloads also increase log volume and token waste when the pulse or workers inspect these values.

## Acceptance criteria
- Move debug output for these helpers off stdout (stderr or gated logging only).
- Keep the helpers' stdout contract strictly numeric.
- Add regression coverage proving clean integer stdout even when debug logging is enabled.

title: Pulse throughput: add review-backlog backpressure and merge prioritization for large PR queues
body:
## Summary
- Worker output is currently producing PRs much faster than the system is draining them through review/merge.
- The open PR backlog is now large enough to become a throughput bottleneck in its own right.

## Evidence
- `gh pr list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --state open --limit 200` returned `200` open PRs.
- Age distribution: `3` within 1h, `30` within 3h, `63` within 6h, `165` within 12h.
- Recent worker telemetry shows substantial successful output, but average effective worker concurrency still remains far below the configured cap, suggesting end-to-end flow is constrained elsewhere.

## Why it matters
- Dispatching more workers into an already-large review queue may reduce end-to-end throughput and increase coordination cost.
- The pulse should likely shift some effort from pure dispatch toward review/merge drain when PR backlog exceeds a threshold.

## Acceptance criteria
- Define backlog thresholds that trigger stronger merge/review prioritization or dispatch backpressure.
- Ensure pulse can detect and act on large PR queues without regressing earlier prefetch bugs.
- Add telemetry so open PR backlog and merge-drain rate are visible alongside worker utilization.

title: Pulse policy: default-open worker eligibility except issues with needs-* labels
body:
## Summary
The current pulse dispatch policy is too restrictive.

Desired policy:
- Every issue and PR should be eligible for worker attention by default.
- The only items that should be skipped by default are those tagged with `needs-maintainer-review` or another `needs-*` label.

## Why this matters
Live review showed a large gap between backlog size and dispatchable work:
- `queued_without_worker` was very high
- `runnable` was often very low
- many issues appear to be excluded by status/assignment/gating logic rather than true blockers

That makes the system look underfilled even when there is abundant backlog.

## Required direction
- Treat worker eligibility as default-open.
- Use real blockers to skip work: `needs-maintainer-review` and other `needs-*` labels.
- Do not let status labels like `status:queued`, `status:in-progress`, or maintainer self-assignment suppress otherwise-valid dispatch when there is no active worker, no open PR, and no live dispatch-ledger entry.
- PRs should remain eligible for worker attention as well; backlog work should not be restricted to issues only.

## Acceptance criteria
- Document the new eligibility rule clearly.
- Update candidate filtering so non-`needs-*` issues/PRs remain dispatchable when they have no real active owner.
- Add regression coverage for items that are currently skipped only because of status/assignment state.
